newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa plans naval diving team for Comoros crash.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans naval diving team for Comoros crash.

text.p: South Africa said on Sunday it would send a navy diving team to the Comoro Islands to help retrieve bodies from a hijacked Ethiopian airliner which crashed in the Indian Ocean.
South African Navy spokesman Stan Slogrove said the request for help had come from the Ethiopian government and the team of divers from Simon's Town was preparing to leave on Sunday night.
"The diving team has been requested to assist with the recovery of bodies of the victims from a piece of the aircraft which is lying under water," Slogrove said in a statement.
At least 67 bodies have been recovered from the Boeing 767 flight ET 961 that crashed on Saturday after it ran out of fuel. Fifty-two people survived and 56 are missing presumed dead.
A team of 15 French rescue divers flew into the Comoros from the Indian Ocean island of Reunion on Sunday.
